specification:
Implement a small configuration language in the package confl. confl/errors.py (read-only, already provided) defines ConfigError(message, line, column), a ValueError subclass with attributes message, line and column. confl/tokens.py defines the namedtuple Token(kind, value, line, column) and tokenize(text); confl/parser.py defines parse(text); confl/__init__.py exports ConfigError, Token, tokenize and parse. Both tokenize and parse raise TypeError when text is not a str. Positions are 1-based; a column counts characters (code points) of the line, and a tab, a carriage return or any other character each occupy one column. tokenize(text) returns a list of Token objects and always ends with one EOF token. Spaces, tabs and carriage returns () separate tokens and produce nothing. '#' outside a string starts a comment that runs up to, but not including, the next line feed (
). Every 
 produces a NEWLINE token (value "
") located at the column of that character, so empty lines give consecutive NEWLINE tokens. The EOF token (value "") is located just after the last character of the text. The other kinds are: LBRACKET, RBRACKET, EQUALS, COMMA, DOT (value is the single character '[', ']', '=', ',', '.'); NAME, which starts with an ASCII letter or '_' and continues with ASCII letters, digits, '_' or '-' (value is the text); INT, which is an optional '-' directly followed by one or more ASCII digits and ends at the first character that is not an ASCII digit (value is the Python int, leading zeros allowed, so 007 is 7 and -0 is 0); and STRING. A STRING starts and ends with a double quote and must be closed on the same line. Inside it a backslash must be followed by one of: another backslash, a double quote, the letter n, the letter t; these stand for a backslash, a double quote, a line feed and a tab. Every other character, including '#', stands for itself. The token value is the decoded text, while the position is that of the opening quote. Tokenizer errors are ConfigError with these positions: an unterminated string (the line ends or the text ends before the closing quote) at the opening quote; an invalid escape (a backslash followed by anything else, by a line feed or by the end of the text) at the backslash; any other unexpected character, including a '-' that is not followed by a digit, at that character. parse(text) returns a new nested dict. A document consists of lines; a line is blank, or a section header, or an assignment, and nothing but a NEWLINE or EOF may follow a header or an assignment on its line. A header is '[' NAME ('.' NAME)* ']' and makes the table named by that path current, creating missing tables along the path (created tables are empty dicts). Assignments before the first header go to the top-level dict. An assignment is NAME '=' value, where the key is a single NAME and is stored in the current table. A value is a STRING (str), an INT (int), the bare words true and false (bool), or a list '[' ... ']' of values separated by commas; a list may be empty, may contain lists and mixed types, may have one trailing comma, and may span several lines (NEWLINE tokens inside brackets are ignored). Any other bare word is an error. A key that already exists in the current table (as a value or as a sub-table) is a duplicate key. Each header path may be written explicitly at most once: a second explicit header with the same path is an error, but a table that so far only exists as an ancestor created by a longer path may still be opened explicitly once, and an explicit header may be followed later by headers of its descendants. A header whose path passes through, or ends at, a key whose value is not a table is an error. Every parse error is a ConfigError located at the token where it is detected, scanning left to right: a duplicate key is detected as soon as its name has been read (position of the key name); a duplicate or conflicting section is detected once the closing ']' of its header has been read and is reported at the opening '[' of that header; for every other violation (unexpected token at the start of a line, missing section name, ']' or '=', missing value, unknown bare word, missing ',' or ']' in a list, extra tokens at the end of a line) the position is that of the offending token, which may be a NEWLINE or the EOF token. Tokenizer errors are raised before any parsing starts, so they take precedence over parse errors elsewhere in the text. Empty text, or text with only blank lines and comments, gives an empty dict.
